findings.title: Grant shortcut matcher rejects the expected shortcut
findings.body: This condition returns `false` when the token ID contains the expected grant shortcut, so events with the correct token ID fail the assertion; it returns `true` for a different shortcut instead. Reverse the condition so the matcher accepts the expected grant and rejects other grants.

findings.title: Decoder assumes every grant shortcut is two characters
findings.body: The grant factory contract describes shortcuts as usually three letters, and custom OAuth2 grant factories can supply their own shortcut, but this decoder requires the entire encoded context to be exactly six characters. A grant using the documented three-character shortcut can produce a token ID that this decoder rejects, preventing the context from being retrieved. Validate shortcut lengths against the format or make the encoding self-delimiting.

findings.title: Constructor fails to reject a null raw token ID
findings.body: This second null check checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result, callers can construct a context with a null raw ID, and encoding it produces an ID ending in the literal `null` rather than rejecting invalid input.
